anomalies.observed: On the Power sheet the TPS2121RUXR power mux (U1) has its output OUT (pin 1) on the VBUS net and its IN2 (pin 2) on the +5V net. On the Microcontroller sheet the USB-C VBUS pin (J10, pin A4) is drawn carrying the VBUS global label AND a +5V power port on the same wire. Because the mux output net (VBUS) and the USB input net (+5V) are tied together at J10, IN2 and OUT of U1 are the same electrical node, shorting the mux output to its own USB input and to the USB VBUS pin.
anomalies.expected: The specification states the mux output VBUS rail is a distinct net from the USB +5V input: 'J12 ... VBUS pins -> +5V net -> U5 pin 2 (IN2)' and 'OUT ... onto the VBUS net ... note this net is named VBUS in the netlist but is distinct from the USB +5V net upstream of the mux.' IN2 should be the USB 5V input and OUT should be the separate pre-buck VBUS rail so the mux can arbitrate between IN1 (+12V) and IN2 (+5V).

evidence.quote: Power sheet (power.kicad_sch): U1 TPS2121RUXR, pin 1 OUT -> VBUS (up arrow), pin 2 IN2 -> +5V
MCU sheet (mcu.kicad_sch): J10 USB_C_Receptacle, pin A4 -> VBUS with a +5V power symbol on the same wire
note this net is named VBUS in the netlist but is distinct from the USB +5V net upstream of the mux

anomalies.impact: The autoswitching power mux is defeated: its output is hard-wired to its IN2/USB-VBUS node. When the 12 V barrel jack is connected, the mux would pass ~12 V onto the node that is also the USB VBUS / +5V rail, back-feeding the host port and over-volting the 5 V side; conversely the buck input (VBUS) is clamped to the USB 5 V, so the board cannot be powered from the barrel jack as intended. Either way the two input supplies are merged instead of being arbitrated.

parsed.summary: The drawing shows a net-name collision that shorts the TPS2121 power-mux output (VBUS) to its USB input (+5V) at the USB-C connector, contradicting the specification's explicit statement that VBUS and +5V are distinct nets; this defeats the supply arbitration and is the one well-supported anomaly.
